patients.species_as_documented: 34-year-old woman with generalized pustular psoriasis and methotrexate-induced cutaneous ulceration
attribution_limitations: The discussion says ulcerations did not localize within psoriatic plaques but appeared on nonlesional skin and mucosa, while the case text describes erosions over pre-existing plaques and the Fig 2 caption describes ulceration of previous psoriatic lesions on the jaw and upper chest.
The text says lesions were limited to the lips (in the context of no intraoral ulcerations), yet a jaw wound was cultured and Fig 2 caption lists jaw, upper chest and upper extremity lesions.
Authors list mild renal dysfunction as a possible contributor yet state she had no known comorbidities; eGFR is 78 mL/min/1.73 m^(2).
The skin biopsy is not dated: it follows the sentence about the June 2024 presentation but the GPP was first diagnosed in 2018.
Serial hemoglobin and platelet values have no printed dates, and the earliest values are not stated to be baseline.
The 2024 MTX course has no stated route in its own sentence; oral appears only for the 2018 course and the Fig 2 caption (oral weekly methotrexate).
The authors describe the case as skin of color; no race or ethnicity is otherwise documented.
